implantation: Neointimal healing reduces the volume of acute stent malapposition with many acute stent malapposition struts becoming completely integrated into the vessel wall However; cases of acute stent malapposition with a volume or acute stent malapposition located within the edges of the stent were not resolved in most cases. Thus; acute stent malapposi tion volume and location within stent edges were identified as independent predictors of late-persistent stent malapposition Our results indicate that an acute stent malapposition with larger volume Or area is more likely to persist at follow-up examinations, which is consistent with findings from previous studies.4,6,8 Late-persistent stent malapposition could be differ entiated from resolved acute stent malapposition by an acute large stent  malapposition area >1.2 mm? according to an IVUS study < A strut-to-vessel distance <260 um on poststent OCT images was suggested as stent malapposition.
